title: UEFA and CONCACAF Demand FIFA Pay $2.1 Billion to Member Associations From Reserves
detail: UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin and CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani sent a joint letter to FIFA president Gianni Infantino demanding a one-off release of at least $10 million to each of FIFA's 211 member associations — roughly $2.1 billion in total — from reserves the two confederations said would reach about $6 billion after the 2026 World Cup. The letter argued 'FIFA already has the capacity to deliver substantially more to its MAs from its own balance sheet — without any sale of interests in its competitions, and without asking anything of the MAs in return,' and called for an independent review of FIFA's finances with full access to the underlying figures and assumptions. The demand is the latest step by UEFA and CONCACAF to pressure Infantino after the collapse of his FIFA Forward Enterprise plan to sell World Cup commercial-rights stakes to private investors.

media.caption: UEFA and CONCACAF demanded FIFA release $2.1 billion in reserves to its 211 member associations

title: German FA Vice-President Watzke: Infantino 'Must Go, No Ifs or Buts'
detail: Hans-Joachim Watzke, a vice-president of the German Football Association (DFB), said at an artificial-intelligence festival in Berlin that Gianni Infantino must leave the FIFA presidency 'no ifs or buts.' Watzke cited three points against Infantino: the FIFA Peace Prize, launched by Infantino and awarded in December 2025 to US President Donald Trump; the reversal of American forward Folarin Balogun's automatic red-card suspension during the World Cup following a phone call from Trump to Infantino; and the FIFA Forward Enterprise plan, unveiled July 28 and dropped four days later, to open a new commercial entity to private investors. The DFB was among the few federations that had not signed a letter of support for Infantino's re-election.

media.caption: DFB vice-president Hans-Joachim Watzke said Gianni Infantino must leave the FIFA presidency 'no ifs or buts'
